breakfast.name: Katogo (Plantain Stew)
instructions: Peel and chop plantains
Sauté onion, garlic, tomatoes
Add meat and plantains
Add water, simmer until tender
breakfast.description: Green plantain stew — Uganda's signature breakfast.

breakfast.name: Rolex (Rolled Eggs)
instructions: Beat eggs with vegetables
Cook omelette on griddle
Place on hot chapati
Roll up tightly
breakfast.description: Egg omelette rolled in chapati — Uganda's street food phenomenon.

breakfast.name: Katogo (Plantain Stew)
ingredients: Green plantains (matooke variety, peeled and chopped)
instructions: Katogo is the Ugandan breakfast stew -- plantains cooked with a protein or sauce
Green plantains are peeled and chopped into chunks
Simmered with beef offal, groundnuts, or beans in a seasoned tomato base
The plantain softens and absorbs the broth
A hearty morning meal -- eaten before a long day of work
Katogo means "mix" -- everything goes in one pot
breakfast.description: Ugandan breakfast plantain stew -- katogo (meaning "mix"), green plantains simmered with offal, groundnut paste, or beans in a spiced tomato broth. A hearty one-pot morning meal.

breakfast.name: Mandazi (East African Doughnuts)
ingredients: Flour, sugar, yeast or baking powder
instructions: Mandazi are the East African fried dough -- eaten across Uganda, Kenya, and Tanzania
A slightly sweet dough flavored with cardamom and coconut milk
Cut into triangles and deep-fried until golden and puffy
Eaten with tea (chai) in the morning
Sold by street vendors and at every market
The cardamom and coconut distinguish East African mandazi from plain doughnuts
breakfast.description: East African fried dough triangles -- mandazi, lightly sweet with cardamom and coconut milk, deep-fried until puffy and golden. Eaten with chai. Sold at every Ugandan market.

lunch.name: Matoke (Steamed Plantains)
instructions: Peel plantains, wrap in banana leaves
Steam until very soft
Mash, make tomato-onion sauce
Serve together
lunch.description: Steamed and mashed green plantains — the Ugandan staple.

lunch.name: Groundnut Sauce
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, tomatoes
Add peanut paste and water
Add chicken if using
Simmer until thick
lunch.description: Rich peanut sauce — served over matoke or rice.

lunch.name: Luwombo (Banana Leaf Steamed Stew)
ingredients: Chicken, beef, or goat (cut into pieces)
instructions: Luwombo is the Buganda royal court dish -- food steamed inside banana leaves
Created by personal chef Kabaka Mwanga II in the 19th century
Meat, groundnut sauce, and vegetables wrapped in banana leaves and slow-steamed
The banana leaf imparts a subtle earthy, grassy flavor
A celebratory dish -- weddings, introductions (kwanjula), and holidays
The groundnut sauce: roasted peanuts ground into a thick paste
Luwombo represents the apex of Buganda cuisine -- reserved for honored guests
lunch.description: Buganda royal court dish -- luwombo, meat and groundnut sauce wrapped in banana leaves and slow-steamed for 2 hours. Created by Kabaka Mwanga II's chef in the 19th century. The banana leaf imparts an earthy flavor. Reserved for weddings and honored guests.

lunch.name: Posho and Beans
instructions: Posho (also called ugali) is the Ugandan maize staple -- cornmeal cooked into a firm porridge
Maize flour stirred into boiling water until it forms a thick, moldable mass
Cut into portions and served alongside beans, stew, or vegetables
Posho and beans: the everyday Ugandan lunch -- affordable and filling
The beans are cooked in a tomato-onion sauce
A meal that feeds the nation -- from school canteens to worker lunches
lunch.description: Ugandan everyday staple -- posho (firm maize porridge) served with red kidney beans in tomato sauce. Affordable and filling. The meal that feeds the nation from school canteens to worker lunches.

lunch.name: Groundnut Stew (Ebinyebwa)
instructions: Groundnut stew (ebinyebwa) is central to Ugandan cuisine
Roasted groundnuts pounded or ground into a thick paste
The paste is dissolved in broth and simmered with meat and vegetables
Rich, creamy, and nutty -- the groundnut flavor permeates everything
Served over posho, matooke, or rice
Uganda is a major groundnut producer -- peanuts are woven into the cuisine
The stew thickens as it cooks -- the groundnut oil separates and floats to the top
lunch.description: Ugandan groundnut (peanut) stew -- ebinyebwa, roasted peanuts ground into paste, dissolved in broth, simmered with meat and vegetables until rich and thick. The groundnut oil separates to the top. Uganda is a major peanut producer. Served over posho or matooke.

dinner.name: Luwombo (Banana Leaf Stew)
instructions: Make sauce with peanuts, tomatoes, mushrooms
Wrap meat and sauce in banana leaves
Steam 2 hours
dinner.description: Meat steamed in banana leaf packets — a Buganda royal dish.

dinner.name: Tilapia from Lake Victoria
instructions: Season fish with lemon
Fry until golden
Make tomato sauce
Serve with matoke or posho

dinner.name: Tilapia (Fried Whole Fish)
instructions: Tilapia is the freshwater fish of Lake Victoria -- the world's largest tropical lake
Uganda borders Lake Victoria and the fish is a dietary staple
The whole fish is scored, seasoned, and fried until crispy-skinned
Served with a tomato-onion relish
Eaten with posho or sweet potatoes
The fishing communities around Lake Victoria depend on tilapia and Nile perch
dinner.description: Ugandan Lake Victoria tilapia -- whole freshwater fish scored, seasoned with curry powder, and fried crispy. Served with tomato-onion relish. Lake Victoria is the world's largest tropical lake; its fishing communities depend on tilapia and Nile perch.

dinner.name: Matooke (Steamed Green Bananas)
ingredients: Green bananas (matooke variety -- starchy, not sweet)
Groundnut sauce or meat stew (for serving)
instructions: Matooke is the Ugandan national dish -- steamed green bananas
A specific variety of starchy banana (East African Highland banana)
Peeled, wrapped in banana leaves, and steamed until soft and mashable
Mashed into a smooth, starchy consistency
Served as the starch base with groundnut sauce, meat stew, or vegetables
Matooke is the staple of the Baganda people and central Uganda
The banana plant is so central to Ugandan life that the word for food in Luganda is related to bananas
dinner.description: Ugandan national staple -- matooke, starchy green bananas (East African Highland variety) peeled, wrapped in banana leaves, and steamed until soft and mashable. Served with groundnut sauce or stew. The banana plant is so central that the Luganda word for food relates to bananas.

dinner.name: Muchomo (Roasted Meat Skewers)
ingredients: Goat meat or beef (cut into cubes)
instructions: Muchomo is Ugandan roasted meat on skewers -- the street food staple
Meat (usually goat) threaded on wooden skewers and roasted over charcoal
Seasoned simply with salt
Served with chilli sauce and sometimes kachumbari (tomato-onion salad)
Sold at roadside stands and bars in the evening
The charcoal flavor is essential -- gas or oven roasting is not muchomo
A social food -- eaten while drinking at bars (locally called rolex joints)
dinner.description: Ugandan charcoal-roasted meat skewers -- muchomo, goat or beef cubes on wooden sticks, salt-seasoned, roasted over charcoal. Sold at roadside stands and bars in the evening. The charcoal flavor is essential. A social food eaten while drinking.

snacks.name: Mandazi (East African Doughnuts)
instructions: Mix dough, rise
Shape triangles
Fry until golden

snacks.name: Rolex (Egg Chapati Roll)
ingredients: Chapati (flat wheat bread, fried on a griddle)
instructions: The Rolex is Uganda's most famous street food -- a rolled egg chapati
The name: "rolled eggs" said fast becomes "rolex"
A chapati is placed on the griddle, a beaten egg poured over and cooked
Fresh vegetables (tomato, onion, cabbage) placed on top
Rolled up like a wrap -- eaten immediately, hot from the griddle
Invented in the 2000s by Kampala street vendors
The rolex has become a national food icon -- there was even a UNESCO petition
snacks.description: Uganda's most famous street food -- the Rolex (rolled eggs, said fast), a fried egg omelette wrapped in chapati with fresh vegetables. Invented by Kampala street vendors in the 2000s. A national food icon. Hot off the griddle.

snacks.name: Samosa (Fried Triangular Pastry)
ingredients: Filling: seasoned ground beef or lentils with onion, chili, cumin
instructions: Samosas in Uganda reflect the Indian trading influence in East Africa
Indian traders have been in East Africa since the 1800s, bringing samosas along
The Ugandan version uses spiced ground beef or lentils
Wrapped in thin pastry, folded into triangles, and deep-fried
Sold at every market and street corner
Eaten as a snack with hot chilli sauce
snacks.description: Ugandan samosas -- spiced ground beef or lentils wrapped in thin pastry triangles and deep-fried. Reflects Indian trading influence in East Africa since the 1800s. Sold at every market with hot chilli sauce.

snacks.name: Sim Sim Balls (Sesame Seed Balls)
instructions: Sim sim balls are the Ugandan sesame seed sweet
Toasted sesame seeds mixed with hot sugar syrup and formed into balls
Crunchy, sweet, and nutty
A traditional snack made at home
Sim sim (sesame) is widely grown in northern Uganda
A portable energy snack -- taken on journeys and given to children
snacks.description: Ugandan sesame seed candy -- sim sim balls, toasted sesame mixed with sugar syrup and formed into crunchy sweet balls. Sesame (sim sim) is widely grown in northern Uganda. A portable energy snack for journeys.

desserts.name: Kashata (Coconut Peanut Bar)
instructions: Cook sugar until caramelized
Add coconut and peanuts
Pour onto tray, let harden
Break into bars

desserts.name: Kashata (Coconut Candy)
instructions: Kashata is the East African coconut candy -- crunchy and sweet
Sugar caramelized with coconut until it sets into brittle squares
Sometimes colored pink or green
Sold in small packets at shops and markets
A childhood treat across East Africa
desserts.description: East African coconut candy -- kashata, sugar caramelized with desiccated coconut and set into brittle squares. Sometimes colored pink or green. A childhood treat across East Africa.

desserts.name: Kabalagala (Banana Pancakes)
instructions: Kabalagala are Ugandan banana pancakes -- ripe bananas mixed with cassava flour
The cassava flour gives a slightly chewy texture different from wheat pancakes
Pan-fried in small rounds until golden
Sweet from the ripe bananas -- minimal added sugar needed
A dessert or afternoon snack
The combination of banana and cassava is distinctly Ugandan
desserts.description: Ugandan banana pancakes -- kabalagala, ripe mashed bananas mixed with cassava flour and pan-fried into golden rounds. The cassava gives a chewy texture. Sweet from the bananas. Distinctly Ugandan combination.

drinks.name: Bell Lager
instructions: Serve cold

drinks.name: Bushera (Millet Drink)
instructions: Cook thin millet porridge
Add malt, cool
Ferment 1-2 days
Serve cold

drinks.name: Bushera (Fermented Millet Drink)
instructions: Bushera is the Ugandan fermented millet drink from western Uganda
Millet flour cooked into a porridge, then mixed with sorghum malt for fermentation
Left to ferment for 1-3 days -- slightly sour and fizzy
A traditional drink of the Bakiga and Banyankole people
Nutritious -- consumed as both a drink and a meal
Low alcohol (like kvass or kombucha) -- drunk by all ages
The sorghum malt provides the enzymes for fermentation
drinks.description: Ugandan fermented millet drink -- bushera, finger millet porridge fermented with sorghum malt for 1-3 days. Slightly sour and fizzy. Traditional to the Bakiga and Banyankole people of western Uganda. Low alcohol, drunk by all ages. Both a drink and a meal.
